purpose: Public sequential question/evidence/decision register. Raw experimental assets remain private.

entries.question: Can the Kaggle Gemma environment load the intended model, capture the correct text MLP tensors and preserve execution semantics?
entries.question_provenance: Retrospective summary of preserved engineering runs; not a newly preregistered question.
entries.method: Dependency/model smoke runs, text-versus-media module selection, hook and cache checks; preserve and repair failures.
entries.result: Real text-channel capture became possible after dependency, scope and cache issues. Early failures remain in receipts and compute ledger.
entries.interpretation: Engineering access is necessary but does not identify a functional neuron role.
entries.next_question: Which measured changes correspond to useful behaviour rather than formatting or numerical execution?
entries.direction_decision: Retain the instrumentation; do not repeat smoke tests without a new implementation change or failure.

entries.question: Can verified self-generated code and controlled response-format adaptation produce useful changes in the model?
entries.question_provenance: Retrospective summary; original sources/receipts retain the precise historical conditions.
entries.method: Generate96 solutions, independently verify candidates, compare adaptation objectives and paired activation changes.
entries.result: Accepted 37 of 96 generated solutions, concentrated in two families. On the corrected 12-task development set, the base passed 5 tasks, the full-response adapter passed 6, and the boundary adapter passed 4. No general improvement was established.
entries.interpretation: Data acceptance concentration and response-format confounding require controlled analysis.
entries.next_question: Do position/format effects explain observed activation changes?
entries.direction_decision: Historical training is superseded. Reuse only its infrastructure/lessons; no more adapter training.

entries.question: How do controlled response-position objectives affect activity and development coding scores?
entries.question_provenance: Retrospective summary linked to original result receipt.
entries.method: Position controls, paired prompts/activations and independently graded development code.
entries.result: On 24 development tasks, the base passed 10, the full-response condition passed 14, boundary passed 9, header passed 10, and random passed 11. The full condition had four gains and no losses against base (paired p = 0.125). This was exploratory and inconclusive.
entries.interpretation: Activity drift alone is not useful learning or a functional role.
entries.next_question: Are selected channel groups causally important and more useful than matched random groups?
entries.direction_decision: Move to causal tests; do not optimize these training objectives in the current sprint.

entries.question: Do activation/weight-derived channel groups show reproducible causal coding benefit under ablation?
entries.question_provenance: Retrospective summary of the frozen E02 protocol and complete cross-seed receipts.
entries.method: 338/3380-channel groups, two original adapter seeds, sham and matched random groups; fixed development panels.
entries.result: No replicated steering benefit. A secondary first-seed gain failed to replicate; all conditions remain recorded.
entries.interpretation: Changed channels are not automatically domain-functional units.
entries.next_question: Can native-neuron semantic contrasts and direct causal tests identify bounded functions without training?
entries.direction_decision: Broaden the scientific basis from training-drift groups to native functional localization.

entries.question: Do optimizer-state explanations reproduce the observed weight and activation effects across seeds?
entries.question_provenance: Retrospective summary of frozen diagnostics and replication.
entries.method: Fixed optimizer branches with a second-seed replication and predeclared activation-error criterion.
entries.result: Activation approximation criterion failed at both seeds despite smaller weight differences. No general coding improvement.
entries.interpretation: Optimizer diagnostics did not answer the user's current neuron-function goal.
entries.next_question: Which controls are necessary to distinguish actual neuron effects from numerical effects?
entries.direction_decision: Closed groundwork; no continuation under the hard no-training constraint.

entries.question: Do the frozen historical adaptation conditions transfer to the held-out MBPP panel?
entries.question_provenance: Retrospective summary of the original prospectively frozen confirmation.
entries.method: 128 eligible tasks, five fixed conditions,640 predictions, one frozen host scoring pass.
entries.result: Base56/128; four adapters57,59,56,60. All paired intervals include zero; no reliable positive transfer.
entries.interpretation: The development signal did not establish transfer.
entries.next_question: The new neuron study needs its own prospective fresh confirmation after valid causal and engineering evidence.
entries.direction_decision: CLOSED. Never rerun the scorer, choose edits from these outcomes or reuse its answers for new selection.

entries.question: Can equivalent adapter refactorizations alter execution despite exact repeat/identity controls?
entries.question_provenance: Retrospective summary; frozen protocol and original failed/startup versions preserved.
entries.method: 13 fixed numerical conditions,208 predictions,1820 compact arrays,2460 factor proofs; zero new optimizer updates.
entries.result: Repeat/identity/power-of-two controls exact. Rank permutations perturb some activities/outputs; one development correctness gain is inconclusive.
entries.interpretation: Numerical execution matters; closest prior already reports equivalent-refactorization effects. No novelty or coding improvement claim.
entries.next_question: Can functional neuron edits be validated against exact noops and representation-matched baselines?
entries.direction_decision: Keep the control lesson. Do not let numerical diagnostics displace neuron-function/coding questions.

entries.question: Would fixed causal masks retain their apparent effects under an equivalent numerical refactorization?
entries.question_provenance: Prepared frozen protocol; no GPU results.
entries.method: Prepared fixed-mask numerical crossover; no run in this direction authorized under the current focus.
entries.result: No measurements. Prepared notebooks are not results.
entries.interpretation: Potentially useful diagnostics, but not the strongest current goal.
entries.next_question: Prioritize the human's native-neuron interpretation and direct-edit objective.
entries.direction_decision: Deferred; do not launch simply because source exists.

entries.question: Can native E2B MLP neurons be localized and steered in a controlled patch-choice pilot, and can silent new-neuron/residual-MLP additions preserve actual-model behaviour?
entries.question_provenance: Question summarized from the prospective N01 protocol, frozen before GPU outputs; subsequent no-training scope amendment changed no runtime conditions.
entries.method: 32 discovery prompts and 64 development prompts; 43 fixed conditions and 2,320 decisions. Individual/group gains, random controls, counterfactual patches and silent 8-neuron/64-unit branches. Zero optimizer updates.
entries.result: All 2,320 rows were checked on the host. Both additions preserved all 64 baseline logit hashes. Identity, cached-generation, reload and restoration checks passed within the receipt limits. Runtime: 961.74 seconds; peak allocated CUDA memory: 7.77 GiB; compact output: 18.02 MB.
entries.interpretation: Actual checkpoint compatibility for these two branch forms is established. Physical dense add/delete, full decoder insertion, individual semantic roles and fresh coding improvement are not established.
entries.next_question: Can matched neurons be compared across original floating-point and NF4 representations, and can prescribed permanent edits pass the same engineering and functional controls?
entries.direction_decision: Go deeper on provenance, precision pairing and direct connection surgery. Broaden beyond binary patch choice before a coding-capability claim.

entries.experiment: N02: shared-source precision and physical surgery
entries.question: Can text-only E2B run in unquantized BF16 and same-parent NF4, and can physical deletion, cloning, prescribed addition and permanent connection edits pass explicit equivalence/reload checks?
entries.question_provenance: Direct human request, developed into the N02 protocol and frozen before GPU outputs. Versions 2 and 3 repair inventory and diagnostic logging under dated amendments; conditions and tolerances are unchanged.
entries.method: Two representations of the same pinned floating-point parent. Fourteen conditions on 16 reused development prompts per representation, plus 12 reload measurements: 460 measurements in total. Zero training. Fixed algebra tolerances and exact identity/restoration gates. NF4 physical edits use an explicitly dequantized target MLP and its unchanged dense baseline;the original-to-dense numerical change is recorded separately.
entries.result: Version 3 completed all 460 measurements across unquantized BF16 and same-parent NF4. All hard gates and ten algebra comparisons passed. Deletion matched zeroing, and outgoing-weight doubling matched gain-2 steering exactly on all 16 prompts in each representation. Physical zero-output addition preserved the dense target-layer baseline exactly. BF16 split cloning changed some logits by up to 0.125 but passed the fixed tolerance and preserved top-1 tokens. Peak allocated CUDA memory was 8.95 GiB (BF16) and 7.00 GiB (NF4). Both startup failures remain recorded.
entries.interpretation: Physical editing and custom patch replay now work on the actual pinned text model in both representations within the tested scope:one channel in layer 34 and 16 development prompts. This does not establish a neuron function, new capability, coding improvement or speedup.
entries.next_question: Can a bounded causal neuron role survive changed wording/output formats and transfer to executable coding?
entries.direction_decision: Engineering gate passed. Move to the functional coding study;retain exact and tolerance-qualified comparisons without rerunning N02.

entries.question: Do the N01 selected channels show a specific coding role or mainly change patch-choice confidence?
entries.question_provenance: Posthoc question and contrast plan recorded after all N01 outcomes were read. No prospective semantic claim.
entries.method: Use all existing conditions and selected traces. Compute coordinate overlap, balanced semantic/label/order contrasts, all9 counterfactual comparisons and random-activity matching quality. No model forwards or final data.
entries.result: The three selected counterfactual groups changed margins but produced no answer-choice flips across 48 recipient prompts. Boundary and deduplication groups shared 4 of 8 channels and the same top-ranked channel. Across 48 random-control matches, the median control/selected activity-RMS ratio was 0.102; none were within 10% of the selected activity RMS. All contrasts and controls are retained.
entries.interpretation: N01 does not identify a domain-specific neuron function or establish coding benefit. Margin effects alone are insufficient.
entries.next_question: Can localization at intermediate semantic/code-continuation positions survive new output formats and actual executable coding tests?
entries.direction_decision: Broaden beyond A/Bdecision-token screening. Use closer activity/effect-size controls in the next functional study; do not relabel the pilot as successful interpretation.

entries.question: Do native neurons conditionally support inclusive-boundary coding across reversed comparison forms, and can fixed edits affect executable completions without damaging retention?
entries.question_provenance: Intent followed the N01 control analysis. The exact N03 protocol was frozen before task implementation and GPU outcomes. The host analysis plan was recorded after launch and before retrieving any outputs.
entries.method: Freeze BF16 discovery selection, activity-matched random controls, same-source NF4 coordinate transfer, real-model token-path checks, identity and semantic/self patches. Test every condition on generated Python line completions and division/JSON retention. No training.
entries.result: All 896 outputs and grades passed the host audit. Every condition scored 4/16 threshold, 4/8 division and 8/8 JSON in each representation. No semantic-patch success change or coding gain occurred. All no-op and restoration checks passed.
entries.interpretation: The selected neurons affect internal scores but do not establish a semantic role. Most dominant threshold outputs were outside the token contrast; development wording also omitted explicit integer types. Shared-KV path controls and current/all-position equivalence passed.
entries.next_question: Can typed tasks and a new fixed memory connection reveal native-neuron functions beyond late output readout?
entries.direction_decision: Broaden. Preserve the null and frozen grades. Verify task clarity and connection feasibility before another localization matrix.

entries.question: Can a clean public code checkout reconstruct every released physical edit from the pinned base and match the original weights and development outputs?
entries.question_provenance: Prospective reconstruction check after the human requested saved edited models on GitHub;not a new coding-benefit experiment.
entries.method: Reconstruct all six fixed physical edits in each representation from the published code and pinned base. Compare all available weight hashes and the original outputs on two unchanged N02 development prompts. No new model selection or training.
entries.result: All 24 original output hashes and all 18 previously recorded projection hashes matched exactly. All 36 edited projection hashes are saved in the model bundles. Zero optimizer updates. A separate full-model replay of the N01 public loader remains unverified.
entries.interpretation: The public package reconstructs the N02 models in the pinned T4 environment. This verifies reconstruction, not a semantic role, coding improvement or bitwise portability across platforms.
entries.next_question: Which native neurons compute useful coding distinctions, and can controlled direct edits improve executable outcomes?
entries.direction_decision: Close R01. Return to N03 functional coding. Further routine reconstruction runs are unnecessary.

entries.experiment: N04: typed coding and memory-connection gate
entries.question: Can a prescribed new memory connection make late native neuron activity causally available to later positions and affect typed coding without training?
entries.question_provenance: Proposed after N03 complete null. The GPU protocol was frozen after 30 random-weight CPU cases and task/oracle preflight, before GPU outcomes.
entries.method: Copy full-attention key/value projections from layer 14 into a frozen memory branch at layer 24. Compare nine fixed policies, historical versus current-only values, feature-permuted controls, typed executable continuations, native-neuron interventions and measurement gradients. No training.
entries.result: All 288 records passed the host audit, including 32 carried original outputs, 32 exact off-mode rows, 18 amended cache checks, 54 path interventions, 18 gradient records and 9 restorations. Historical connections make the tested late native activity affect later outputs; original, off and current-only controls retain the exact past-path null. Full K/V and value replacements score zero on all 32 inputs. Quarter-strength key-only gains two of eight division completions with no observed losses; the unadjusted paired p value is 0.5.
entries.interpretation: The architecture changes access to past native activity without training. This is a structural result, not a semantic neuron role. The small key-only effect reuses four function-name pairs and is unconfirmed across multiple conditions. The typed baseline improves on N03 because prompts changed; that is not a model-edit gain. Cache equivalence remains qualified by the weaker dated diagnostic.
entries.next_question: Which native channels transmit a rounding requirement at a shared instruction anchor, and do necessity, opposite-policy patches and rescue change executable function behavior beyond matched random groups?
entries.direction_decision: Close the connection engineering gate and retain the complete grid. Do not select a winning permutation or strength. Move to early native-neuron functional localization; any later connection benefit test must be prospective and retain mild controls.

entries.experiment: N05: native semantic-anchor roles and executable functions
entries.question: Can a small native neuron group at an instruction anchor transmit a rounding policy and causally change correct function behavior without training?
entries.question_provenance: Proposed after the complete N03 and N04 audits. N03 missed dominant alternatives and selected late units. N04 opens their historical path but does not establish a semantic role.
entries.method: Use forward activity at the same punctuation token in six crossed policy strata to select 32 native channels in layers 0 through 13, with nested eight-channel diagnostics and two strict matched random groups. Test 13 fixed policies on 24 new complete-function and retention prompts, plus 24 descriptive discovery outputs. No fitted vectors, measurement gradients or optimizer updates.
entries.result: All 336 outputs, 48 self/rescue rows, 26 restorations and exact identity controls passed the host audit. The baseline scored 1/16 rounding functions, 4/4 filters and 0/4 strict JSON. Every nonidentity condition scored 0/16, 4/4 and 0/4. Selected and matched random interventions caused the same single loss. No role or gain was established.
entries.interpretation: Nine baseline rounding outputs hit the ceiling and fourteen failed the source/execution gate. Baseline JSON values were correct inside forbidden outer fences; this posthoc content diagnostic leaves the strict grades unchanged. Activity contrast did not establish policy transmission. The missing full-vector anchor control and poor baseline prevent a broad conclusion about native neuron function.
entries.next_question: Can a counterbalanced selector task produce reliable executable expressions, and can full native state transplantation at the selector actually change policy before sparse localization?
entries.direction_decision: Broaden and require a prospective baseline-usability gate plus full-state positive controls. Do not repeat or enlarge the sparse punctuation-anchor sweep. Preserve source/format/cap limitations and every null.

entries.experiment: N06: baseline usability and causal-site gate
entries.question: Can a usable counterbalanced mode selector control executable expressions, and is its information causally accessible through full MLP or reused attention-memory states?
entries.question_provenance: Proposed after N05 complete audit and structure diagnosis. It replaces an inadequate full-function assay and adds the missing full-state positive control.
entries.method: Counterbalanced red/blue integer-filter expressions. Gate usable baseline first, then joint full native MLP or reuse-only K/V donor replacements. Same-policy mapping reversal controls label meaning. No sparse localization yet.
entries.result: All 200 outputs and guards passed. Baseline filtering was correct on 16/16 and JSON on 4/4. Joint early-MLP opposite donors transferred all sixteen programs to the opposite policy. Reversed-mapping same-policy donors preserved fourteen of sixteen. Keys, values and joint K/V produced no functional flips. No outputs hit the cap.
entries.interpretation: Joint early MLP opposite donors transfer16/16;reversed-mapping same-policy donors preserve14/16. K/V donors produce no functional flips. All JSON4/4 and no caps. This locates a conditional site, not individual neuron meanings or coding improvement. Four crossed instruction strata with nuisance-name replications, not sixteen algorithms.
entries.next_question: Which individual layers carry the joint early-MLP effect, and where is native-channel localization justified?
entries.direction_decision: Deepen at the measured MLP site. Decompose every early layer with both donor controls before a sparse search. Opposite-policy transfer is control, not coding improvement.
entries.decision: The proposed rounding assay changed to filtering because N05 filter controls were correct on four of four inputs while rounding was correct on one of sixteen. This is a prospective new assay. N05 grades are unchanged.

entries.experiment: N07: individual-layer decomposition of the native MLP site
entries.question: Which of the fourteen early native MLP layers is sufficient for policy transfer beyond a reversed-mapping same-policy donor control?
entries.question_provenance: Proposed after the complete N06 all-condition audit. The joint early-MLP site transfers every tested opposite policy while keys and values do not.
entries.method: All fourteen individual layers, opposite and same-policy actual donors, exact carried original predictions, live original replay, per-layer self hashes and exact restoration. No sparse selection or optimization.
entries.result: All 600 records passed audit, including twenty carried originals, 280 self hashes, twenty identity generations and sixty restorations. Layer 0 switched all sixteen filter programs under both opposite-rule and same-rule donors. Layers 4 and 9 each switched two prompts under opposite donors only, in a single direction/mapping stratum. Other individual-layer donor conditions preserved all sixteen. All JSON controls passed, with no caps.
entries.interpretation: The layer 0 effect fails the reversed-label same-policy control. No individual layer meets the fixed eligibility criterion. This supports conditional label dependence at the tested whole-layer site, not an abstract-rule neuron or coding improvement.
entries.next_question: Can later-layer blocks specifically rescue a fixed label-corruption background using same-rule donor states?
entries.direction_decision: Follow the prospective branch for no eligible layer: fixed block decomposition and counterfactual rescue. Do not choose layer 0 as an abstract semantic site or rank sparse units blindly.

entries.experiment: N08: fixed-block decomposition and conditional rescue
entries.question: Do later native MLP blocks provide rule-specific rescue after a fixed layer 0 label corruption?
entries.question_provenance: Proposed after the complete N07 audit under its predeclared no-eligible-layer branch. Joint early-layer swaps transfer policies, but layer 0 alone follows the label even under a same-rule donor.
entries.method: Six fixed contiguous blocks in layers 1 through 13. Clean opposite/same-rule swaps and a common layer 0 label-corruption background with opposite, same-rule and recipient donors. Sixty existing reference records are carried without completion regeneration.
entries.result: All 660 records passed audit, including sixty carried references, 240 block-self hashes, twenty corrupted identities and sixty-six restorations. Three blocks met the frozen gate. The size/start rule selects layers 5–9: same-rule donors restore 14/16, opposite-rule donors 0/16, recipient donors 16/16 and clean same-rule donors preserve 16/16. All JSON controls pass, with no caps.
entries.interpretation: A controlled conditional block-rescue effect survives same-selector-token donor controls. It is a whole-block result on reused development prompts. It does not establish necessity, sparse neuron meanings, fresh transfer or improvement of the unmodified model.
entries.next_question: Can a small native group within the selected block account for rule-specific rescue beyond strong random controls on new development prompts?
entries.direction_decision: Deepen in the prospectively chosen five-layer block. Freeze discovery scoring and controls before code; use new development prompts and retain fresh confirmation.

entries.experiment: N09: sparse native groups and new-development necessity/rescue
entries.question: Can small native groups in layers 5–9 support controlled rule-specific rescue beyond matched random groups on new prompts?
entries.question_provenance: Proposed after the complete N08 audit. The fixed size/start criterion selected B05_09 from three eligible blocks.
entries.method: Discovery-only full-program influence ranking from old verified self-generated code; strict activity/write/context-delta matching;64/256native groups; new-development full-site gate; selected/random necessity, amplification and conditional rescue; matched top-eight individual diagnostics. Zero training.
entries.result: All 32 activation-gradient measurements, 384 reference-token targets and four exact ordinary/instrumented logit comparisons passed. Native weights stayed frozen, with no parameter gradients. There are 4,622 positive candidates. The highest-ranked coordinate has twelve eligible controls, below the fixed sixteen. The planned stop produced zero new code outputs.
entries.interpretation: No sparse coding effect was measured. Strict matching exposed a rare high-ranked coordinate; the result does not establish a semantic role or a null causal effect.
entries.next_question: Can a separately frozen matchability-limited native group be tested without weakening the control ratios or pool minimum?
entries.direction_decision: Close N09, preserve failure and reuse compact discovery measurements only. Select from control feasibility before any unused development outputs; do not rerun32backwards.

entries.question: Within the controlled block, does a strictly matchable native group show necessity and rescue beyond both random controls?
entries.question_provenance: Prospective continuation after N09 planned discovery stop; unused development outputs remain unseen.
entries.method: Reuse saved discovery measurements. Bounded deterministic exclusion of control-infeasible selected candidates; all ratio limits, pool minimum, seeds, downstream conditions anddecision rules unchanged. Replay native captures before new outputs.
entries.result: All 168 full-site records passed the frozen audit. The original filter baseline is 16/16; corruption 0/16; same-rule full rescue 12/16; opposite 0/16; recipient 16/16. Arithmetic is 4/4 throughout. JSON is 0/4 throughout because the model returns objects instead of the requested strings. The planned retention gate stopped before any sparse intervention.
entries.interpretation: The controlled block effect transfers to changed development wording. The retention baseline is unusable for that requested output shape. This is not edit-induced retention damage and no individual-neuron effect was tested.
entries.next_question: With one separately frozen clarification of JSON output wording, do the unchanged sparse controls show necessity and rescue?
entries.direction_decision: Preserve every original grade. Carry all 140 unchanged code/arithmetic records exactly; generate only new JSON gate completions and the previously unexecuted sparse panels.

entries.experiment: N11: native-neuron necessity with clarified retention wording
entries.question: After clarifying the requested JSON output shape, do the fixed native groups show controlled necessity and rescue?
entries.question_provenance: Prospective wording-only continuation after N10 stopped at its retention gate. Sparse outcomes were unseen when the protocol was frozen.
entries.method: Keep all selected/control groups, filter/arithmetic prompts, grading, conditions and criteria fixed. Change only four JSON instruction suffixes to previously usable wording. Carry 140 unchanged completions exactly and verify their live logits. Maximum 1,012 new outputs.
entries.result: All 1,152 records audited: 1,012 new and 140 exact carried. The selected 256-neuron group restores two corrupted programs and causes four losses when cut from full rescue, versus zero for both random groups. The primary four-rescue threshold and direction/mapping coverage fail. All 48 individual conditions match their respective baselines and random controls. Every main condition retains 4/4 JSON and 4/4 arithmetic; no caps.
entries.interpretation: A limited conditional group effect, not a passing functional-role candidate. The cut measures dependence within an engineered full-rescue context. Clean zero/double gains do not improve original-model correctness. Individual meaning, useful benefit and novelty remain unestablished.
entries.next_question: Does the originally highest-ranked rare coordinate show a reproducible, context-specific effect under within-unit controls and direct weight edits?
entries.direction_decision: Close this predefined matchable-group test. Preserve all failures and do not promote secondary outcomes. A rare-unit study needs its own prospective scope and cannot claim unavailable matched between-unit specificity.

entries.experiment: N12: rare native unit and permanent connection edits
entries.question: Does the originally highest-ranked rare native neuron carry a context-specific rule signal, and do prescribed permanent edits improve fresh development code?
entries.question_provenance: Prospective separate estimand after N11 failed primary. The original highest-ranked rare coordinate and this alternative route predate N11 output access.
entries.method: One fixed native neuron, actual within-unit counterfactual values and balanced shuffled donors; anchor and global gains; prescribed outgoing-column assignments. Four coding families and eight unchanged retention inputs were planned.
entries.result: All 40 baseline records were audited: 32 new and eight exact carried originals. Filtering and predicates each scored 8/8. Extremum and rounding each scored 0/8. All eight retention cases passed. The validity and per-family guards stopped the run before any edit.
entries.interpretation: This is a planned baseline stop, not an intervention null. No neuron or weight edit was executed. The original code and output-format failures remain unchanged.
entries.next_question: With unchanged prompts and grades, does the neuron affect the two usable rule tasks, and do prescribed edits improve any of the four coding families?
entries.direction_decision: No further wording repairs. Carry all forty originals exactly. Declare the narrower role cohort before interventions and retain every family for coding gains and losses.

entries.experiment: N13: fixed native unit on usable rule domains and all coding outcomes
entries.question: Within the two usable rule domains, does the fixed neuron carry a controlled rule signal, and do prescribed connection edits improve coding?
entries.question_provenance: Prospective narrower scope after N12 baseline-only stop. No neuron-intervention outcomes available. Development baseline selection explicitly acknowledged.
entries.method: Carry all forty N12 originals exactly. Keep all sixteen conditions, prompts, graders and strengths. Use the sixteen filtering and predicate cases for the role question, and all thirty-two coding cases for gains and losses. Verify live baseline and native-capture hashes before edits.
entries.result: All 640 records were audited: 600 new and forty exact carried originals. Every condition has the same correctness. Opposite donors switch none of the sixteen usable rule programs. All permanent edits execute and restore correctly. Stored-column and global activity factors zero and two agree exactly across eighty comparisons.
entries.interpretation: The recorded activity tracks the rule, but this native scalar is insufficient to transfer it under the fixed donor swaps. Zeroing or doubling it gives no coding gain or loss on this panel. Logit and some raw-text changes do not establish a useful function.
entries.next_question: Does a whole native site support contextual-rule transfer on these unchanged prefixes before further sparse localization?
entries.direction_decision: Close the rare-unit test without new strengths or coordinate reselection. Validate a full-site positive control in the broader semantic context before claiming a localization failure or constructing new neurons.

entries.question: Does the fixed rare neuron track the requested relation or the selector label in its recorded prefix activity?
entries.question_provenance: Posthoc description of N12 captures, completed before N13 intervention-output access. Does not change N13 conditions or thresholds.
entries.method: Exactly decompose each four-cell label-by-definition mapping table into its mean, label effect, mapping effect and rule interaction. No fitted vector, model update or new forward call. Check identical selector-state hashes across four later task domains.
entries.result: The rule interaction accounts for 95.05% and 99.11% of centered four-cell activity energy in the two instruction wordings. Every later task domain has the same selector value and full native MLP hash for a fixed prefix.
entries.interpretation: A bounded descriptive association with the contextual comparison rule. The selector precedes task text, so this site cannot distinguish those later domains. No individual semantic function, necessity or coding benefit follows from activity alone.
entries.next_question: Do actual counterfactual and prescribed connection interventions produce rule-specific executable changes?
entries.direction_decision: Keep N13 unchanged and await its complete frozen causal panel. Do not reselect the coordinate or promote this posthoc association to a confirmed role.

entries.question: Can a whole native site transfer the contextual rule in the unchanged coding tasks?
entries.question_provenance: Prospective scope check after the complete N13 null. No N14 implementation or outputs existed when its protocol was frozen.
entries.method: Keep every prompt, grade and base completion. Compare actual opposite-rule and reversed-label same-rule donors at layer 0, layers 5 to 9 and layers 0 to 13. Use exact self, identity and restoration guards.
entries.result: All 400 records audited, including forty carried originals. Layers 5 to 9 transfer the opposite rule in 14/16 usable programs and preserve all 16 under reversed-label same-rule donors. All eight retention cases pass. Layer 0 transfers under both donor types and fails the control; layers 0 to 13 preserve only 13/16 under same-rule donors and fail the threshold.
entries.interpretation: The declared block passes whole-site conditional sufficiency across two coding families. This does not identify individual neuron meanings or a useful model edit. The complete grid includes one incidental development coding gain, which is not confirmed. A posthoc syntax check finds thirteen of the sixteen block-opposite outputs differ only by a strict comparison polarity after fence and bound-variable normalization. Same-rule donors preserve thirteen raw strings, two normalized syntax trees and one equivalent Boolean formulation. This describes saved programs and does not establish a neuron meaning or change the frozen gate. The six incidental condition-level gains concern only two existing extremum cases, both requesting the higher value; they are not six independent replications.
entries.next_question: Which individual layer or adjacent pair within the validated block can pass the same semantic controls?
entries.direction_decision: Follow the frozen positive-site branch. Use a new prospective forward layer/pair grid, retain every control and carry the necessary full-site originals exactly. No re-ranking from a single secondary gain.

entries.question: Which next intervention would resolve a functional uncertainty rather than repeat a sparse null?
entries.question_provenance: Conditional proposals recorded while N14 is active and before its output access. Not a frozen GPU experiment.
entries.method: Compare forward site decomposition, current-readout controls and prescribed neuron-source connections against exact closest priors and the no-training constraint. Require source/position/cache and gain-equivalent controls before construction.
entries.result: Reviewed primary abstracts and selected methods show direct precedents for activation steering, generated-token steering, shared/local history and internal-state augmentation. No new model call, learned vector or GPU launch occurred.
entries.interpretation: A new causal route alone is not a useful new capability. Candidate construction still lacks the native functional evidence required by its trigger.
entries.next_question: Which branch of the frozen N14 decision rule is supported by its complete audited grid?
entries.direction_decision: Keep N14 unchanged. Use its outcome to select the already stated site-or-anchor branch. Do not start a construction sweep merely because an activity signal is large.

entries.experiment: N15: semantic layer and adjacent-pair decomposition
entries.question: Which single layer or adjacent pair inside the validated native block can transfer the contextual rule while preserving same-rule behavior?
entries.question_provenance: Prospective positive-site branch after N14 complete audit. No N15 code or pretrained outputs exist at protocol freeze.
entries.method: All five single layers and four adjacent pairs inside layers 5 to 9 receive actual opposite and reversed-label same-rule donors. Keep all forty inputs and grades. Carry two hundred necessary parent-control records exactly, with live logit replays.
entries.result: All 920 records audited, with 720 new outputs and 200 exact carried parent records. Single-layer transfers are 0, 0, 0, 0 and 4 of 16. Adjacent-pair transfers are 0, 0, 3 and 6. Every same-rule condition preserves all sixteen programs; all eight retention cases pass throughout. No candidate meets the predefined gate.
entries.interpretation: The whole-block result has not localized to any tested single layer or adjacent pair. Partial transfers do not establish an individual neuron role or coding improvement. This supports testing the missing combinations; it does not prove a formal high-order interaction.
entries.next_question: Which remaining layer subset inside the validated block can pass the unchanged semantic gate?
entries.direction_decision: Follow the frozen no-eligible-site branch. Test all remaining combinations once, keep all parent conditions, and use fewest layers then fixed lexical order rather than highest score.

entries.question: Which remaining native layer subset inside layers 5 to 9 passes the unchanged semantic donor controls?
entries.question_provenance: Prospective no-eligible-site branch after all N15 outputs and guards pass. No N16 implementation or outputs exist at protocol freeze.
entries.method: Test the six nonadjacent pairs, all ten triples and all five four-layer subsets. Preserve all forty inputs and grades, actual opposite/same-rule donors and the fixed role gate. Carry 200 necessary common parent records exactly.
entries.result: All 1,880 records were audited, including 1,680 new outputs and 200 exact carried parents. Across all 31 nonempty subsets, no singleton or pair passes the gate. Five triples pass. The prescribed smallest-cardinality and lexicographic selection is layers 5, 6 and 9: opposite-rule transfer in 8/16 cases, same-rule preservation in 16/16 and all eight retention controls correct. Every guard passes, with zero backward passes and updates.
entries.interpretation: Conditional rule transfer is localized to a three-layer site on reused development prompts. This is sufficiency under donor interventions, not individual neuron meaning, formal synergy, necessity or original-model improvement. A later posthoc reading found matching filter/predicate outcomes in every prefix cell. The selected site transfers lower-mode requests in wording 0 and higher-mode requests in wording 1; it fails the opposite direction in each wording. Balanced marginal counts do not establish complete rule invariance.
entries.next_question: Which native channels inside layers5,6,9 carry the controlled donor effect?
entries.direction_decision: Keep every one of the 31 subset outcomes. Queue prospective channel partitions, necessity/rescue and matched random controls after the requested behavior pilots. Do not select a higher-scoring triple.

entries.question: Do prescribed native-neuron edits change conversational behavior, and do those changes coincide with coding degradation?
entries.question_provenance: Direct human suggestion to chat with edited Gemma, supported by a screenshot offered as an unverified lead. No chat outputs exist when this panel and assessment rubric are prepared.
entries.method: Twelve fixed first prompts and four followups compare baseline, identity and whole-conversation zero/double edits of the fixed rare unit and two same-layer random controls. Natural histories and fixed baseline histories separate dialogue feedback from the current edit. Four unchanged coding probes measure retention.
entries.result: All 192 records pass raw-token, carry, scope, identity, counter and restoration audits. There are 158 new predictions, 16 exact closed-parent carries and 18 within-run reuses. All 160 chat records were rated before unblinding, using 55 exact-content groups. Edits change wording but every condition scores 4/4 coding; bounded false-premise, uncertainty and name-memory checks all pass. Twelve or thirteen of twenty chat records per condition are capped.
entries.interpretation: No clear personality shift or coding improvement is established. Qualitative scores are exploratory observer judgments, not an independent validated trait instrument. Random controls also change wording and are not activity matched. The high cap rate limits conclusions.
entries.next_question: Does the separately frozen reversal grid alter coding or conversation under normal and reversed text?
entries.direction_decision: Close B01. Preserve every reply, all conditions and blinded ratings. Proceed with the fixed small reversal pilot; do not reroll or select a dramatic quote.

entries.experiment: B02: neuron and text reversal controls
entries.question: What changes under precisely defined native-neuron reversals and normal/reversed user text, when every answer is read both ways?
entries.question_provenance: Direct human proposal; mathematical definitions recorded before implementation or model results.
entries.method: Four fixed model operations by normal or reversed user code points, using eight unchanged prompts. Both answer readings are retained. The planned 64 records contain 56 new generations and eight exact B01 base carries, giving 128 derived readings. Host algebra, scope and restoration checks pass.
entries.result: All 64 records pass, with 56 new predictions, eight exact carried originals and 128 derived readings. All 64 chat readings were rated before unblinding. Original and aligned reversal score 4/4 coding on normal prompts. Every other model/input/reading cell scores 0/4. Unmatched reversal and sign inversion produce unusable chat in this panel. All 48 restorations and parameter guards pass; zero backward passes and updates.
entries.interpretation: Coordinated reversal preserves ideal algebra but is not numerically bit-identical: all sixteen first-logit hashes differ, while first tokens agree. It changes one normal-input reply and six reversed-input replies, without changing coding correctness. Unmatched reversal and sign inversion do not create a semantic inverse; reversing the displayed answer does not restore the tested behavior. This is a small capped development panel.
entries.next_question: Can native channels in the selected three-layer site support specific causal function and useful coding edits?
entries.direction_decision: Close B02 and retain every model/input/reading cell plus the startup failure. No new reversal strengths or prompt edits from these outcomes. Return to Q31 native-channel coverage, necessity, rescue and matched controls.

entries.experiment: N17: matched native-channel necessity and transfer
entries.question: Which small native post-gating groups within the already validated layers 5, 6 and 9 site causally mediate the conditional rule transfer, and do prescribed edits improve clean coding?
entries.question_provenance: The prescribed next branch follows the complete N16 subset audit. It returns to the native-neuron goal after the requested behavior pilots.
entries.method: Forward-only activity contrasts select 96 native post-gating coordinates in layers 5, 6 and 9. Two fixed random groups match activation RMS, outgoing-column norm and paired donor-change RMS. Fixed actual-donor swaps, clean gains 0 and 2, exact rescue and conditional transfer cuts separate the causal questions. Nine individual-unit sentinels are also tested. There are zero optimizer updates.
entries.result: All 1,002 records pass, including 708 new predictions, 120 parent carries and 174 baseline-reference rescues. Selected and both random groups produce zero opposite-rule transfers, zero clean-role losses and zero conditional-transfer losses. Same-rule preservation is 16/16 for all. All nine individual-unit sentinel arms match their controls. Retention passes throughout.
entries.interpretation: All three primary causal criteria fail. Six condition-level incidental gains concern the same extremum instance, also improved by a random amplification arm and the inherited full donor. There is no confirmed coding improvement or individual semantic function. A prospective arithmetic erratum corrected fixed call overhead from 646 to 546 before output access; every original record remains preserved.
entries.next_question: Can a fixed broader native-channel partition locate the inherited full-vector donor effect before further sparse ranking?
entries.direction_decision: Close N17 without new strengths, re-ranking or reruns. Broaden to prescribed native-channel coverage while preserving all matched nulls and the wording-by-direction limits of the parent site.

entries.experiment: N18: task-informed position and native-channel coverage
entries.question: Does moving observation and intervention after the coding task strengthen causal policy control, and can a prescribed broader channel partition locate that effect?
entries.question_provenance: N17 null and its pre-result interpretation options require broadening beyond a prefix that has not read the task.
entries.method: Use the same forty inputs at the final prompt position. Require a controlled full-site donor gate first, then compare all four magnitude-stratified native-channel quarters with same-rule donors, clean gains, exact rescue and conditional cuts. Zero training.
entries.result: All 160 records pass: 80 new outputs, 40 exact original carries and 40 baseline references. Opposite full-site end-position donors transfer 0/16; same-policy preserves 16/16, and all eight retention cases remain correct. Forty self-logit checks, twelve paired cached hashes and eight restorations pass. Quarter selection and intervention never run.
entries.interpretation: This is the predeclared full-site gate stop. It does not establish that the neurons have no function. The final prompt position and the comparison decision during code generation are different computational contexts.
entries.next_question: Can an actual native code-decision state provide a controlled causal observation site without supplying the divergent answer token?
entries.direction_decision: Keep N18 closed. Validate native-prefix alignment and exact current-step intervention feasibility on the host before freezing another study. Do not expand N18 layers, weaken its gate or run its quarter stage.

entries.question: Can native neurons at the actual generated comparison decision support controlled function, rather than activity at an earlier prompt position?
entries.question_provenance: N18 planned full-site stop motivates checking a later computation where the model actually chooses a comparator.
entries.method: Edit exactly one cached code-decision forward after a native prefix shared across three contexts. Compare fixed neuron L9C4632 and existing controls 850/6085 under actual donor swaps, clean gains 0 and 2, and rescue. Full 35-layer current-state controls and eight activation-gradient measurements are predeclared. No profile selects an intervention. There are 19 conditions and 399 records; retention donor cells are non-applicable references.
entries.result: N19 version 1 stopped before any inference because raw repetition_penalty was None rather than explicit 1.0. Zero model forwards, edits or predictions. A source-only repair resolves the pinned library defaults and rejects nontrivial processors. Version 2 is the one active private job, with protocol and all scientific conditions unchanged. No N19 scientific output has been accessed.
entries.interpretation: Thirteen role cases include eleven exact same-token controls and two same-direction lexical variants. They reuse development contexts with correct baselines, so this assay cannot demonstrate improved original accuracy. Gradients are measurements, never updates. Fixed controls are not activity matched.
entries.next_question: Can the current-step primitives preserve exact identity/cache behavior and isolate only declared scalars?
entries.direction_decision: Keep the single frozen job unchanged. At terminal, verify final source/privacy and input manifest, pull compact outputs once, and run its frozen raw-output and scope auditor. Fixed controls are not activity matched; no original-accuracy gain can be established on these correct baselines.
